document.title: Cable from Secretary of State: Letter to President from Prime Minister Gandhi
document.authors: Secretary of State (transmitting letter from Rajiv Gandhi)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Text of Gandhi's January 7, 1987 letter to Reagan. Gandhi says the USSR wants to withdraw in a realistic time-frame, accuses Pakistan of exploiting Afghanistan to acquire arms such as AWACS, and laments Reykjavik's breakdown.

Gandhi letter to Reagan of 7 January 1987
key_claims: Gandhi says India favours an independent, nonaligned Afghanistan and an early peaceful settlement.
Gandhi reports that Gorbachev indicated the Soviet Union would withdraw forces in a realistic time-frame from a nonaligned, not unfriendly Afghanistan.
India alleges Pakistan is exploiting the Afghan situation to acquire higher levels and types of arms with little bearing on the Afghan border.
India warns that supplying AWACS to Pakistan would trigger a new phase of the arms race.
India states Pakistan's clandestine, military-controlled nuclear weapons programme is the source of regional proliferation risk.
Gandhi accuses Pakistan of assisting terrorists in India and links this to drug trafficking.
